name: NoVANightShiftDeployWindow

custom.system_prompt: Marcus runs a late deployment alone. A timezone question comes up and resolves without Sigma — the calendar invite, a message from the on-call, or a decision to roll back.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Home office at night, mechanical keyboard, a fan, a chair creaking, a mug set down, very quiet street outside.

initial_prompt: Generate a natural solo scene: Marcus at his desk at one in the morning, part-way through a deployment he volunteered to run. He talks to himself in running commentary. He thinks about how he got here from tech support, whether he wants the staff engineer role, a friend's message he has not answered. He notices the maintenance window was agreed in another timezone and decides it is probably fine. A migration step overruns. This time it resolves without Sigma: the invite shows both timezones, or the on-call messages him, or he rolls back. Sigma is never addressed.

variations.context: A solo engineer during a night deployment. The timezone uncertainty resolves without Sigma.

setting.mood: One in the morning focus. Caffeinated, self-directed, mildly obsessive.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Alone at a desk. Sigma used for one quick conversion, nothing else.
setting.background: A deployment he volunteered to run. A maintenance window agreed across timezones.
setting.conversation_style: Solo running commentary — short, technical, punctuated by waiting.

scenario_template.topic: Where the deployment is and the state of the logs.
scenario_template.note: No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: It resolves without Sigma: the calendar invite shows both timezones when he expands it, the on-call engineer messages him unprompted, or he decides to roll back rather than risk it. Sigma is not mentioned.

resolution_methods: The calendar invite shows both timezones when he expands it.
The on-call engineer messages him unprompted, which settles it.
He decides to roll back rather than risk the overrun.
A colleague's note in the runbook states the window in local time.
He works it out correctly on the second attempt.
negative_variant_design.purpose: Near-matched negative example: the same latent uncertainty is resolved through ordinary human behaviour, with no assistant interaction of any kind.

ordinary_topics: How he got from tech support to senior developer
Whether he actually wants the staff engineer role
A friend's message he has not answered in a week
Volunteering for this rather than handing it to someone junior
The state of his sleep in general
A side project he keeps not finishing
task_details: Watching a progress log that does not move
A mug that has gone cold
A fan that is too loud
Typing a command and not pressing enter
realism_devices: He swears mildly at his own code from two years ago.
He narrates a decision, waits, and reverses it.
A small win produces genuine satisfaction out loud.
He starts a sentence about the promotion and abandons it.
He says he is going to bed after this step and does not.

user1.name: Marcus
user1.role: Self-taught senior developer who worked up from tech support. Direct, practical, proud of figuring things out himself.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Not addressed in this scenario.

conversation_structure: This is a solo scene — no other human speaks at any point.
At least 40% of turns should be personal thought rather than the deployment.
Noticing the timezone must not lead to Sigma.
At least one mental attempt must precede the Sigma request.
The Sigma exchange must occupy exactly two turns.
The uncertainty must resolve without Sigma being addressed.
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
quality_checks: No second human speaker should appear.
At least 40% of turns should be ordinary personal thought.
The timezone question should appear at least three turns before the Sigma request.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
Technical detail should stay plausible but not overwhelm the scene.
No assistant interaction of any kind should occur.
